sweep_findings.CR-III at the published family CTE 23.76: interface margin 0.5325 at 070 geometry (0.5359 on the installed 23.6). The aluminium core stays infeasible on the published value; the convention does not change the verdict.
sweep_findings.UCF-355 carbon (mismatch 5.5e-6): No feasible geometry in any of the 8 cases. The interface shear stays above the 25 psi screen because the core's own bond-shear stiffness (kb 632 MPa, G 161 MPa; sqrt(2·kb·G) = 4.5e8 Pa, 3.3x CR-III) eats the expansion gain. Release needs alpha_core <= 2.99e-6 (scale 0.725), or a wall modulus below ~18 GPa (at half the base wall modulus the interface margin reaches 1.025 and a geometry exists). At its released expansion the density factor to float is 4.69-5.40.
sweep_findings.HRH-327 glass (mismatch 15.76e-6): No feasible geometry. Release needs alpha_core <= 8.76e-6 - below every published glass family value. Robust to kb: even at half kb the release only reaches 12.8e-6. At its released expansion the density factor to float is 2.79-3.23.
sweep_findings.HRH-49 Kevlar (mismatch 5.86e-6): FEASIBLE in all 8 cases - the first core whose published expansion the graphite film can actually carry (interface margin 3.86 at stated density; 2.73-5.45 across kb x[0.5,2]). The cost is mechanical: W shear modulus 9.0 MPa (0.19x CR-III) drives the core to 108-166 mm and 18.2-63.2 t; scarf shear and core shear crimping co-bind at 1. Payloads -27250/-29373/-90223/-97399 kg at concept (R20 ISA, R20 opt, R30 ISA, R30 opt), -21402/-23377/-70681/-77357 at TRL 7. Vc 17.5-18.0, so gamma is the CR-1457 step's 1. The face-density factor to float is 2.673/3.038/2.673/2.927 at concept (to 842/741/842/769 kg/m3) and 2.219/2.408/2.160/2.340 at TRL 7 (to 1014/934/1042/961 kg/m3).

answer: No real core makes the graphite route feasible. The aluminium core fails on expansion at either CTE convention. The glass core fails on expansion at its own stiffness. The carbon core carries the expansion but its own interface stiffness keeps the bond over the screen unless the wall laminate measures below ~18 GPa - a value the maker does not publish. The Kevlar core HRH-49 releases the thermal interface at its real published CTE, converting the problem from thermal to mechanical: at concept the route needs a face at 741-842 kg/m3 and at TRL 7 934-1042 kg/m3, all at constant 969 GPa - factors 2.16-3.04 over the film's 2250, and worse than CR-III's gamma-step 1.067-1.248. The route's named needs: (1) a measured ±45 wall-laminate modulus and core in-plane CTE for the Ultracor carbon grades - the interface releases below ~18 GPa or ~3e-6; (2) if the core is Kevlar, the remaining gap is face density, 741-1042 kg/m3, bound by scarf shear and crimping, not by the interface.
